task.title: Spike: run the Python engine in the browser with Pyodide
task.description:
## Why
The site will be static files, with the engine running in the visitor's browser and calling Sleeper directly. Pyodide is Python compiled to WebAssembly. If it runs the existing engine fast enough, the TypeScript port is not needed. This spike measures that before any port work starts.

## Steps
1. Build a throwaway page that loads Pyodide in a Web Worker (a browser background thread) and loads the `rebuild` engine into it.
2. Feed it one league's recorded inputs from the local `cache/` folder. Do not commit league data.
3. Run a full report in the browser and show it on the existing trade board.
4. Confirm the output matches the CLI's `board-data.json` and `summary.json` for the same inputs.
5. Measure, on a desktop and on a mid-range phone profile (slowed CPU and network):
   - download size of the runtime and the engine
   - time from page load to the engine being ready, on a first visit and on a repeat visit
   - time to build one report, and peak memory
6. Measure the other unknown: how long JavaScript takes to fetch one uncached league season from Sleeper with the calls made in parallel.
7. Record the numbers and a recommendation as a comment on this task: keep Python in the browser, or port to TypeScript. Starting rule: keep Python if the runtime adds about 3 seconds or less to a first visit on the phone profile.
8. Prune the backlog to match the decision:
   - Python kept: delete the stories labelled `port-if-needed`.
   - Port chosen: delete "Package the Python engine to run in the browser" and make "Run a report in a background thread with progress" depend on "Assemble the full report pipeline and pass end-to-end parity" instead.

## Done when
- The comment holds the measurements, whether the outputs matched, and the decision.
- The backlog holds only the stories for the chosen path.

comments.author: dylan@dgoings.com
comments.body:
## Result

The unchanged Python engine runs in the browser under Pyodide 314.0.8 (Python 3.14), in a Web Worker, and its output is byte-identical to the CLI's: `board-data.json`, `brief.md`, `trade-board.html`, and `summary.json` apart from its timing fields. The page stayed at 60 frames a second while the worker computed.

Test case: one 12-team Superflex league, five seasons, in season. Measured in headless desktop Chrome on a Mac. "Phone" means CPU slowed 4x with DevTools' network presets; "slower phone" is 6x. No real phone and no Safari were tested.

### Download (brotli, first visit only)

| File | Size |
|-|-|
| Pyodide runtime (wasm, standard library, loader) | 5.9 MB |
| Engine bundle (`rebuild/` and benchmarks) | 134 KB |
| numpy, if loaded | +2.9 MB |

numpy is not needed. With it replaced by an empty stand-in the output is identical, because only the offline benchmark builder calls it.

### Page load to engine ready

| Profile | First visit | Repeat visit |
|-|-|-|
| Desktop (local server, so no real download time) | 0.9 to 1.4 s | 0.8 s |
| Phone, fast 4G (9 Mbps) | 9.3 s | 3.5 s |
| Phone, slow 4G (1.6 Mbps) | 34.7 s | 3.6 s |
| Slower phone, fast 4G | 11.3 s | 5.7 s |

### One report (trimmed player file)

| Profile | Uncached league | Cached league | Memory |
|-|-|-|-|
| Native Python, for comparison | 0.30 s | | |
| Desktop | 0.65 s | 0.42 s | 62 MB |
| Phone | 2.7 s | 1.8 s | 62 MB |
| Slower phone | 4.2 s | 3.4 s | 62 MB |

With Sleeper's full 15 MB player file the same report took 4.4 s on the phone profile and used 209 MB. The engine needs 9 of the file's 53 fields (`age`, `birth_date`, `fantasy_positions`, `full_name`, `injury_status`, `last_name`, `position`, `team`, `years_exp`). Trimmed to those it is 2.2 MB, or 315 KB compressed. That list comes from one league, so check it against the fixture set.

### Pulling an uncached league from Sleeper in the browser

Five seasons, 210 calls, no 429 responses. The CLI takes about 24 s for the same pull, one call at a time.

| Profile | Calls at once | Time |
|-|-|-|
| Desktop | 8 | 3.2 s |
| Desktop | 24 | 0.5 s |
| Phone, fast 4G | 8 | 2.3 s |

The later runs may have been helped by Sleeper's CDN cache.

## Recommendation

Keep Python in the browser for launch, behind one "data in, report out" call so a TypeScript engine can replace it later.

Against the starting rule (about 3 seconds added on a first visit on the phone profile), the raw number misses: 9.3 s. What a visitor waits for is smaller, because the runtime can load while they type a username and pick a league, and while the league is fetched. On fast 4G that leaves roughly 2 to 3 seconds more than a TypeScript engine would take, nearly all of it report compute. The TypeScript figure is an estimate, not a measurement.

Where it is clearly worse:
- A first visit on a slow connection: about 35 s before any report can start.
- A first visit that lands directly on a report link, with no typing time to hide the load.
- Every report on a phone takes 2 to 4 s to compute.

What it buys: no port (ten stories), identical results by construction, and one engine shared with the CLI.

## Follow-ups for the stories that build on this

- Make `import numpy` in `rebuild/metrics.py` lazy, so the browser never downloads it.
- Start loading the runtime as soon as the landing page opens.
- The spike replays recorded HTTP through a stand-in for `requests`. The real build needs "Separate the engine from fetching".
- Test on a real phone and in Safari before launch.

## Waiting on

The keep-or-port decision. The backlog has not been pruned yet. The spike code is in `spike/pyodide/` on branch `spike/pyodide-engine`, uncommitted. Recorded league data is in `cache/spike/`, which is gitignored.
